discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 170920
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
520 AM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Widespread frost is expected Saturday night into Sunday
  morning with a potential of temperatures dropping to the
  freezing mark, especially east of IN-15. A frost advisory and
  freeze warning have both been hoisted.

- After the below normal temperatures this weekend, temperatures
  rebound back above normal for much of next work week with dry
  weather expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 304 AM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

Surface high pressure continues to build in causing low level 
moisture to dissipate, lake induced instability to wane, and low 
level trajectories to become more southerly. As lake enhanced rain 
dissipates early this morning, dry air takes over and we're in this 
dry pattern for the foreseeable future. This is as the upper jet 
retreats into MI and upper ridging builds into areas east of the 
Rockies. An area of low pressure washes out between Wednesday and 
Thursday as a cold front pushes southeastward ahead of another 
surface high. The ECMWF has rain approaching the area, but that's 
really the only model that does so. 

Otherwise, the temperatures are the most noteworthy piece of 
weather that should be discussed here. Morning temps fell back 
into the 30s this morning, but lingering wind and limited 
decoupling restricted frost formation to patchy at best despite 
temperatures falling into the mid 30s and even some low 30s in 
some outlying spots. 850 mb temps this morning reached around 
-2C and, even as that aforementioned return flow takes over, we 
have our lowest temperatures of this young cool season as 
freezing temperatures look to settle in along and south of 
US-24. The give and take between surface high pressure-affected 
weak flow and encroaching strengthening gradient to our north 
and west once again lessens confidence on frost formation on the
northern side of our freeze watch for Sunday AM. There are 
signs in forecast soundings of a decoupling boundary layer Sun 
AM and again Mon AM, although lesser confidence in frost occurs 
Monday and even lesser for Tuesday. While WAA doesn't appear to 
be established in the following days, temperatures are forecast 
to trend warmer, rising above 40 degrees by Wednesday AM. Highs 
surpass 70 degrees again Tuesday morning, although a few areas 
in White, Pulaski, Cass, and Fulton could achieve 70F Monday as 
well.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 520 AM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

High pressure builds in with VFR conditions, light winds and
mainly clear skies this weekend into much of next week. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT this morning for INZ005>009-014-
     017-104-116-204-216.
     Frost Advisory from 3 AM EDT /2 AM CDT/ to 9 AM EDT /8 AM CDT/ 
     Sunday for INZ005-012>015-020-022-103-104-203-204.
     Freeze Warning from 3 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for INZ006>009-017-
     018-023>027-032>034-116-216.
OH...Freeze Warning from 3 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for OHZ001-002-004-
     005-015-016-024-025.
MI...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT this morning for MIZ078>081.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 11 AM EDT this morning for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 170514

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1214 AM CDT Sat Oct 17 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected today.

   ...Synopsis...
   In the wake of a cold frontal passage, much of the CONUS will be too
   dry and stable for thunderstorm development today. The front will
   continue moving southward along the central/southern FL Peninsula,
   where scattered storm development will be possible within a very
   moist environment. Poor lapse rates and weak deep-layer shear should
   limit organized severe potential, though localized strong gusts may
   occur. Across the Southwest, sporadic lightning flashes may
   accompany weak convection associated with a slow-moving mid/upper
   low centered offshore of Baja California.

   ..Dean/Chalmers.. 10/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 170545

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1245 AM CDT Sat Oct 17 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected tomorrow (Sunday).

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level ridge will remain over the central U.S. while a 500 mb
   cut-off low meanders off of the Atlantic Coast and broad upper
   troughing dominates the western CONUS tomorrow (Sunday). A
   relatively cool and stable low-level airmass will overspread much of
   the CONUS, inhibiting thunderstorm development. A few thunderstorms
   may occur over the southern FL Peninsula, where the heating of
   remnant low-level moisture will promote localized lift and buoyancy.
   A couple of lightning flashes may also occur over portions of the
   Desert Southwest, where cooler temperatures aloft and modest ascent
   will accompany a weak mid-level impulse.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 170716

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0216 AM CDT Sat Oct 17 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level cut-off low will continue to meander off of the Atlantic
   Coast while an upper trough deepens over the Interior West and an
   upper ridge remains in place over the central U.S. on Monday. A cool
   and/or stable low-level airmass will remain in place over most of
   the U.S., limiting thunderstorm development. However, the
   amplification of the western upper trough will promote low-level
   moisture return beneath cooling temperatures aloft over the Desert
   Southwest, increasing the chance for thunderstorms in this area. A
   thunderstorm or two may also occur over the far southern FL
   Peninsula, in tandem with the heating of some residual low-level
   moisture.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/17/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
